slides.text:
A function is a value. You can keep it in a variable, hand it to another function and call it later. The variable holds a **function pointer**.

Pseudo code, not Rust.
slides.code:
op = the function double
op(5)  ->  runs double with 5

slides.text:
The type of a pointer is the signature of the functions it can hold: the parameters and the return type. Only a function with exactly that signature fits.

Use the bare name to hand a function over. With parentheses it runs and you get its result.

exercises.title: Keep a function in a variable
exercises.guide: Store a function in a variable, call it through the variable, then point the variable at another function.

chunks.guide: `main` is already in the file. A function that doubles a number.
A second function with the same signature: it flips the sign.
Keep `double` in a variable and call it through the variable.

notes.text: The type: any function taking an i32 and returning an i32
Only the name: the function is not called here

chunks.text:
let mut op: fn(i32) -> i32 = double;
    println!("{}", op(21));

chunks.guide: Point the same variable at the other function and call it again.

notes.text: A mut variable can hold a different function later
